editorial:
Imagine moving into a huge apartment in St. Petersburg and finding out your mirror is a doorway to another version of your own home. That is the fun starting point of this movie, where quiet Alisa meets party-loving Ivan through a strange reflection. Their worlds feel close but never quite touch, which gives the story a sweet, playful energy. You get cozy apartment scenes, funny misunderstandings, and a romance that builds through glances and small moments rather than big speeches. The fantasy idea is easy to follow, so you can relax and enjoy the charm instead of untangling complicated rules.

The leads have good chemistry, and the mirror scenes are the most fun part, especially when both apartments start reacting to each other. The pacing is mostly brisk, though a few middle scenes slow down while the couple keeps circling the same problem. If you like light romantic comedies with a magical twist, you will likely have a great time. It is best watched with someone you can nudge during the sweet moments, and you can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for movie night.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Alisa and Ivan finally figure out how to sync their two apartments through the mirror. The twist is that true love is what makes the glass doorway stable, not just the strange magic. They reach through at the same moment, their worlds merge, and they finally touch in real life. The movie ends with them stepping into one shared apartment, leaving the parallel reality behind, and starting their relationship in the same world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cozy romance with a magical twist.
